items.title: Merit, Office, Old Age, and Awakening Are All Earned Alike — Doctrine Fourteen Closes

items.zh: 若善不善，若王若臣，若機捷，若增進滿足。若為王顧錄以為給侍，若不顧錄。若是老病死法，若非老病死法。若修梵住已，生於梵世，若復不爾。若修菩提分法，若不修習。若悟聲聞菩提、獨覺菩提、無上菩提，若復不爾。
items.en: So too with performing wholesome or unwholesome deeds; with becoming a king or a minister; with being quick-witted or eloquent; with prospering and growing satisfied through one's own effort; with being taken into a king's service, or not; with being subject to old age, sickness, and death, or rising above them through genuine practice; with cultivating the four divine abodes and being reborn into Brahmā's own heavenly world, or not; with cultivating the factors of awakening, or not; and with realising the awakening of a śrāvaka, a pratyekabuddha, or the unsurpassed awakening, or not realising any of them at all.

items.zh: 又汝何所欲？為從勝種類生，此名為勝？為由戒聞等耶？若由從勝種類生者，汝論中說：於祠祀中，若戒聞等勝，取之為量。如此之言，應不中理。若由戒聞等者，汝先所說諸婆羅門是最勝類，餘是下類，不應道理。如是產生故，作業故，受生故，工巧業處故，增上故，彼所顧錄故，梵住故，修覺分故，證菩提故，戒聞勝故，不應道理。是故此論非如理說。
items.en: Further, what do you actually intend: does birth into a supreme caste itself constitute superiority, or is it moral discipline and learning that constitute it? If birth alone constitutes superiority, then your own scriptures' instruction — that whoever excels in discipline and learning should be selected to officiate at sacred rites — should make no sense at all. If discipline and learning constitute it instead, then your earlier claim that brahmins are supreme by caste while other castes are inferior makes no sense. Therefore, this doctrine is not a soundly reasoned teaching.

items.title: The Fifteenth Doctrine: Mistaking Heavenly Bliss and Meditative Absorption for Nirvana Itself

items.zh: 妄計清淨論者，謂如有一，若沙門、若婆羅門、起如是見，立如是論：若我解脫，心得自在，觀得自在。謂於諸天微妙五欲堅著攝受，嬉戲娛樂，隨意受用，是則名得現法涅槃，第一清淨。
items.en: The doctrine of false purity: there are certain renunciants or brahmins who hold such a view and establish such a doctrine — that once I am liberated, once my mind attains mastery and my perception attains mastery, this is called purity. That is: clinging to and reveling in the heavens' exquisite sensual pleasures, sporting and delighting in them, freely indulging as one wishes — this, they say, is attaining nirvāṇa in this very life, the highest purity.

items.zh: 又有外道，起如是見，立如是論：若有離欲惡不善法，於初靜慮得具足住，乃至得具足住第四靜慮，是亦名得現法涅槃，第一清淨。
items.en: Further, other non-Buddhist teachers hold such a view and establish such a doctrine: that abiding fully in the first dhyāna, having become free of desire and unwholesome states, up through abiding fully in the fourth dhyāna, likewise constitutes attaining nirvāṇa in this very life, the highest purity.

items.title: Sacred Rivers Wash Away Sin, and Seven Ascetic Vows Bring Purity

items.zh: 又有外道起如是見，立如是論：若有眾生，於孫陀利迦河沐浴支體，所有諸惡皆悉除滅。如於孫陀利迦河如是，於婆湖陀河、伽耶河、薩伐底河、殑伽河等中沐浴支體，應知亦爾，第一清淨。
items.en: Further, other non-Buddhist teachers hold such a view and establish such a doctrine — that should any being bathe their limbs in the Sundarikā River, every one of their sins is thereby entirely washed away. And just as with the Sundarikā River, so too, it should be understood, with bathing one's limbs in the Bāhukā, Gayā, Sarasvatī, or Ganges rivers — this too is the highest purity.

items.zh: 復有外道，計持狗戒以為清淨，或持牛戒，或持油墨戒，或持露形戒，或持灰戒，或持自苦戒，或持糞穢戒等，計為清淨。
items.en: Further, other non-Buddhist teachers hold the vow of a dog to be purifying, or the vow of a cow, or the vow of smearing oneself with lampblack, or the vow of going naked, or the vow of covering oneself in ash, or the vow of self-mortification, or the vow of consuming filth, and hold each of these to be purifying.

items.zh: 謂說現法涅槃外道，及說水等清淨外道作如是計。問：彼何因緣，起如是見，立如是論？答：由教及理故。教如前說。理者：謂如有一，為性尋思，乃至廣說。彼謂得諸縱任自在、欲自在、觀行自在，名勝清淨。然不如實知縱任自在等相。又如有一，計由自苦身故，自惡解脫；或造過惡，過惡解脫。

items.title: Four Dilemmas Dismantle Every Claim to False Purity

items.zh: 今應問彼：汝何所欲？若有於妙五欲嬉戲受樂者，為離欲貪？為未離耶？若已離者，於世五欲嬉戲受樂，不應道理。若未離者，計為解脫清淨，不應道理。又汝何所欲？諸得初靜慮、乃至具足住第四靜慮者，彼為已離一切貪欲？為未離耶？若言一切離者，但具足住乃至第四靜慮，不應道理。若言未離一切欲者，計為究竟解脫清淨，不應道理。
items.en: One should press them: what do you actually intend — is one who sports and delights in the heavens' exquisite pleasures free of craving for desire, or not yet free? If already free, then still sporting and delighting in worldly sensual pleasure makes no sense. If not yet free, then holding this to be liberation and purity makes no sense. Further, what do you intend regarding those who abide in the first dhyāna up through fully abiding in the fourth — are they free of all craving, or not? If entirely free, then merely abiding in any of the four dhyānas, rather than something higher still, makes no sense. If not entirely free of all craving, then holding this to be final, ultimate liberation and purity makes no sense.

items.zh: 又汝何所欲？為由內清淨故究竟清淨？為由外清淨故究竟清淨？若由內者，計於河中沐浴而得清淨，不應道理。若由外者，內具貪瞋癡等一切垢穢，但除外垢、便計為淨，不應道理。
items.en: Further, what do you intend — is ultimate purity a matter of inner purity, or outer purity? If inner, then holding that bathing in a river achieves purity makes no sense. If outer, then still harbouring craving, hatred, and delusion within while merely removing outward dirt and calling this "purity" makes no sense.

items.zh: 又汝何所欲？為執受淨物故而得清淨？為執受不淨物故得清淨耶？若由執受淨物得清淨者，世間共見狗等不淨，而汝立計執受狗等得清淨者，不應道理。若由執受不淨物者，自體不淨而令他淨，不應道理。
items.en: Further, what do you intend — is purity achieved by taking on something pure, or something impure? If by taking on something pure, then, since the whole world plainly recognises a dog's habits as impure, your claim that imitating a dog achieves purity makes no sense. If by taking on something impure, then something impure in itself producing purity in another makes no sense.

items.zh: 又汝何所欲？諸受狗等戒者，為行身等邪惡行故而得清淨？為行身等正妙行故得清淨耶？若由行邪惡行者，行邪惡行而計清淨，不應道理。若由正妙行者，持狗等戒則為唐捐，而計於彼能得清淨，不應道理。
items.en: Further, what do you intend — do those who take up the vow of a dog achieve purity through wrongful, unwholesome conduct, or through genuinely wholesome conduct? If through wrongful conduct, then wrongful conduct producing purity makes no sense. If through genuinely wholesome conduct, then the entire vow of imitating a dog is simply wasted effort, achieving nothing that ordinary wholesome conduct does not already achieve.

items.zh: 如是離欲不離欲故，內外故，受淨不淨故，邪行正行故，不應道理。是故此論非如理說。

blocks.text: Today finishes the refutation of caste supremacy and then examines the fifteenth doctrine: false ideas of purity. These include the belief that heavenly pleasure or meditative absorption is already nirvāṇa, that bathing in sacred rivers washes away sin, and that imitating dogs or cows leads to heaven. The treatise's answer locates purity in the mind.
Untranslated: 0312b14–b21 (those who teach nirvāṇa in this life and purity by water hold this; why they hold it) and 0312c15–c17 (a summary of why false purity fails).

Are only the other castes born of parents? Everyone sees brahmins born of mothers too. Every caste equally needs the three conditions for conception (Day 6). Every caste does the same work, gains the same offices, grows old, and can attain awakening. Any caste can "cultivate the divine abodes and be reborn in Brahmā's world"; Venerable Miào Jìng explains the divine abodes as love, compassion, joy, and equanimity.

The final dilemma: does superiority come from birth or from discipline and learning? The brahmins' own scriptures say the officiant at rites should be chosen for his discipline and learning, so by their own texts, superiority lies there and not in birth. Master Cháng Bǎi notes that the Buddha himself spoke of "true brahmins", meaning those of right conduct, as a skilful way to speak to Indians in their own terms.

The fifteenth doctrine includes the **five "nirvāṇas in this life"**: revelling in heavenly sense pleasure, and abiding in each of the four dhyānas. Master Cháng Bǎi: they think the first dhyāna frees them from sorrow, the second from pain, the third from joy, the fourth from pleasure, and mistake release from a feeling for release from saṃsāra. Venerable Miào Jìng: "mastery of mind" can be said of arhats and Buddhas, but here it means only mastery of desire or of meditation.

Some hold that bathing in the Ganges or other sacred rivers washes away every sin. Others keep the "dog vow" or "cow vow", eating filth or grass like those animals. Master Cháng Bǎi explains why: "in absorption they observed a dog die and be reborn in heaven", and imitated it. Others smear themselves with soot or ash, go naked, or lie among fires.

Venerable Miào Jìng names the root error: "Fundamentally, what keeps you from liberation is affliction, not sin. It isn't past wrongs that bind you; it's your afflictions." Washing the body cannot reach them.

items: Is the one revelling in pleasure free of craving? If so, why still revel? If not, how is it liberation?
Is purity inner or outer? If inner, bathing is irrelevant. If outer, "still harbouring craving, hatred, and delusion within while merely removing outer dirt" is not purity.
Does purity come from taking on something pure or impure? Everyone sees a dog's habits as impure.
Are dog-vow keepers purified by wrong or right conduct? If by right conduct, Master Cháng Bǎi concludes, "the dog and cow vows are wasted effort"; purity comes from the right conduct itself.

blocks.text: Self-mortification is not questioned again here because, as Master Cháng Bǎi notes, it was already refuted on Day 46.

quiz.q: The first dilemma: are only other castes born of parents, or brahmins too? If only others, what's wrong?
options: everyone sees brahmins born of mothers too — it denies plain fact
quiz.why: "If only the other castes, then this plainly contradicts what everyone can see: brahmins are plainly born from their mothers too — denying plain fact makes no sense." Master Cháng Bǎi: "Everyone can see all brahmins are born of mothers; saying otherwise slanders plain fact." If brahmins are the same, supremacy collapses.

quiz.q: The final dilemma: does superiority come from birth or from discipline and learning? If from birth, why is it self-contradictory?
options: their own texts say the officiant at rites should be chosen for excellence in discipline and learning — so superiority lies there, not in birth
quiz.why: "If birth alone constitutes superiority, then your own scriptures' instruction — that whoever excels in discipline and learning should be selected to officiate at sacred rites — should make no sense at all." Master Cháng Bǎi: "The officiant must be learned and pure in precepts, or the rite has no merit." If discipline and learning decide, brahmin supremacy fails.

quiz.q: According to the treatise, what does the first group of false-purity theorists take as nirvāṇa in this life?
options: clinging to and reveling in the heavens' exquisite sensual pleasures
quiz.why: "Clinging to and reveling in the heavens' exquisite sensual pleasures, sporting and delighting in them, freely indulging as one wishes — this, they say, is attaining nirvāṇa in this very life, the highest purity." Venerable Miào Jìng: gods "just enjoy the five pleasures, nothing else." Master Cháng Bǎi on Delighting in Transformation: a thought, and it appears.

quiz.q: How are the "five nirvāṇas in this life" counted, according to the teachers?
options: the four dhyānas as four, plus the desire heavens' sensual enjoyment as one — five
quiz.why: Venerable Miào Jìng: "The four dhyānas make four; add the six desire heavens and you have the 'five nirvāṇas in this life.'" Master Cháng Bǎi: "Adding the desire heavens' mastery of pleasure gives five." (The reading note counts four heavens plus one dhyāna — the reverse; logged in the correction list.)

quiz.q: According to the treatise, by what means do some outsiders think all sins are washed away?
options: bathing in the Sundarikā, Bāhukā, Gayā, Sarasvatī, or Ganges rivers
quiz.why: "Should any being bathe their limbs in the Sundarikā River, every one of their sins is thereby entirely washed away. And just as with the Sundarikā River, so too … with … the Bāhukā, Gayā, Sarasvatī, or Ganges rivers." §29 refutes it with "inner or outer purity."

quiz.q: According to Venerable Miào Jìng, what is the root reason one isn't liberated — so bathing and austerity don't help?
options: the root is affliction, not sin — it's not past wrongs that keep you bound, but your afflictions
quiz.why: Venerable Miào Jìng: "Fundamentally, what keeps you from liberation is affliction, not sin. It isn't past wrongs that bind you — it's your afflictions." So "Buddhists should avoid pointless austerity and work hard at the foundations of mindfulness to cut affliction."

quiz.q: The text asks whether ultimate purity is inner or outer. If outer, what's wrong?
options: harbouring greed, hatred, and delusion within while merely removing outer dirt and calling it purity makes no sense
quiz.why: "If inner, then holding that bathing in a river achieves purity makes no sense. If outer, then still harbouring craving, hatred, and delusion within while merely removing outward dirt and calling this 'purity' makes no sense." This dilemma targets sacred-river bathing.
